answer: Each agent carries a ferrous‑signed token minted by a hardware enclave and must embed a unique cryptographic quill‑stamp in every protocol message. When a new identity appears, surrounding nodes query a vine‑shaped trust graph that records recent quill‑stamps and requires a proof‑of‑work cost proportional to the depth of the graph; a Sybil batch would need to generate a distinct ferrous token and solve thousands of work puzzles. The total expense grows linearly with the number of fake identities, making large‑scale attacks economically infeasible.
